metaData.originalTitle: MOSS 全模态技术体系全解析：统一离散化建模、推理优化与情境数据构建路径
metaData.title: Complete Analysis of the MOSS Full-Modal Technology System: Unified Discrete Modeling, Inference Optimization, and Contextual Data Construction Pathways
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Through an exclusive interview with Mosi AI founder Qiu Xipeng, this article delves into the MOSS full-modal technology system, covering the definition of Context Intelligence, unified discrete modeling, inference optimization, and high-quality contextual data construction, revealing the evolution direction of multimodal AI architecture.
metaData.summary: This article is an in-depth interview by InfoQ with Professor Qiu Xipeng, a Fudan University professor and founder of Mosi AI. As the publisher of China's first conversational large language model MOSS, Qiu systematically elaborates on the technical path of 'Context Intelligence' he proposed. The article first defines Context Intelligence as the inevitable direction for large model development, encompassing five stages: perception, representation, delivery, persistence, and feedback loop. It then details the architecture design and collaboration mechanisms of the MOSS series sub-models: MOSS-Audio (general audio understanding), MOSS-VL (video understanding), and MOSS-TTS (high-fidelity speech synthesis), emphasizing a unified representation centered on discrete tokens. On technical challenges, Qiu analyzes how to address computational pressure from context expansion from three levels: representation compression, model architecture, and inference system, and compares the essential differences between 'full-modal unified discrete modeling' and mainstream 'bridge-style' approaches. Addressing data bottlenecks, the article proposes constructing high-quality contextual data through synthesis pipelines and world models, pointing out that data processing pipelines are the core differentiation barrier among models. Finally, Qiu summarizes the practical references the MOSS series provides for the industry in three aspects: approach, methodology, and ecosystem, emphasizing the role of open-source strategies in driving ecosystem prosperity.

mainPoints.point: Context Intelligence is the inevitable direction for large model development, with the core being expanding the depth and breadth of input dimensions.
mainPoints.explanation: Qiu Xipeng believes large models have three expandable directions (pretraining scale, inference path, input dimensions), and Context Intelligence focuses on the latter, emphasizing unified processing of multimodal information such as text, speech, image, and video, as well as external information like user preferences and physical scenes.

mainPoints.point: Full-modal unified discrete modeling achieves representation unity by converting signals from different modalities into discrete tokens.
mainPoints.explanation: Unlike traditional 'bridge-style' approaches, the MOSS series preserves each modality's characteristics at the tokenization layer but fully shares the language model paradigm in downstream model layers, thereby improving scalability and training efficiency.

mainPoints.point: Inference optimization addresses the computational pressure from context expansion through three concurrent approaches: representation compression, model architecture, and system-level improvements.
mainPoints.explanation: Audio is compressed to 12.5 Hz frame rate, video uses variable frame rate sampling to reduce token consumption; MOSS-VL decouples visual encoding from inference decoding; KV cache compression achieves over 90% reduction through low-rank modifications, making long-context deployment feasible.

mainPoints.point: The primary source of high-quality contextual data is the synthesis pipeline and world models.
mainPoints.explanation: Given the high cost of real-world multimodal data collection, Qiu proposes a three-step method: design scenarios using text-based large models, convert them into multimodal data, then perform fine-grained annotation. He also explores building simulation sandboxes through world models to autonomously generate contextual data.

mainPoints.point: Data processing pipelines are the core differentiation barrier among models.
mainPoints.explanation: As models evolve toward complex contexts, the ability to accumulate and process long-trajectory, multimodal, high-complexity contextual data will determine the actual performance gaps between models.

keyQuotes: Future intelligence depends on the expansion of more complex 'Context' inputs.

The core of a full-modal unified architecture is 'representation unity': using discretization technology to convert continuous signals such as speech, image, and video into discrete symbols similar to text.
Data has always been the most core source of differentiation between different models.
We have verified that the path of 'unified representation' is feasible and yields clear benefits.
The industry will ultimately move in this direction; it is an inevitable law of large model development.

relatedArticles.title: JD.com Ad Large Model in Practice: How the GRAM Architecture Delivers Generative Recommendations in Under 50ms
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: JD.com's advertising team unveils the GRAM architecture, which achieves generative recommendations within 50ms by directly aligning intent with product semantics, employing fast and slow dual-pathways, leveraging knowledge engineering, and optimizing engineering, while effectively mitigating hallucinations.

relatedArticles.title: Integrating UI Generation into the Pipeline: Semi-Supervised Evaluation for Automated UI Production
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article shares Ant Group's engineering practices in generative UI, transforming UI generation from a technical capability into an engineering capability that can be integrated into a production pipeline by building a prompt workbench, requirement rewriting, component detection, style management, streaming rendering, and an automated review system.

relatedArticles.title: GLM-5.2 Released and Open-Sourced: Focused on Coding and Long-Horizon Tasks
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Zhipu AI released and open-sourced GLM-5.2, focusing on Coding and long-horizon tasks. It achieved first place globally in the Code Arena blind test, and with its 1M context and open-source SOTA performance, it is now the strongest open-source Coding model.

relatedArticles.title: A Comprehensive Guide to Microsoft Build 2026: The 'Agent-First' Era Arrives with Seven In-House Models
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Microsoft Build 2026 unveiled seven in-house MAI models, the Scout agent, the MXC system-level security sandbox, and Project Solara, marking the full implementation of an 'Agent-First' strategy.

relatedArticles.title: Pushing Large Models to the Billion-DAU Frontline: How Kuaishou Live Reconstructs Matching Efficiency and Interactive Experience
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how Kuaishou Live leverages large model technologies, including its self-developed KVL multimodal architecture, reinforcement learning aligned with user preferences, AI-generated host introductions and broadcasts, and interactive agents, to reconstruct matching efficiency and interactive experience in a billion-DAU scenario, resulting in a 4.1% revenue increase.

relatedArticles.title: LLM Training You Didn't Know: Principles, Paths, and New Practices - Tw93
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article systematically outlines the full-stack architecture of LLM training in 2026, providing an in-depth analysis of key technical decisions and engineering practices ranging from pre-training, data engineering, and post-training to Agent training and Harness optimization.

relatedArticles.title: AI R&D Automation: Wiki Knowledge Base + Skill Pack
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article details how to build a continuously growing team knowledge base and a supporting expert skill pack based on the LLM-Wiki model and the Obsidian platform to achieve AI-driven R&D automation.

relatedArticles.title: After Consuming Hundreds of Billions of Tokens: Reflections on Software Construction, Forms, and Future Development in the Agent Era
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on a speech by Huang Dongxu, CTO of TiDB, at QCon, this article shares his deep reflections on software production, forms, and future trends in the Agent era after consuming hundreds of billions of tokens. Core viewpoints include code becoming an execution carrier, the democratization of software production, the evolution of software forms towards intent interfaces, and the future emergence of complex abstractions beyond Skills.

relatedArticles.title: CIOs Are Abandoning AI Code Generation Rate: A Practical Review of What Truly Counts as R&D Efficiency
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Based on a year of practical experience, the Alibaba Cloud CIO team proposes that the core of R&D efficiency in the AI era lies in 'scaling' rather than 'code generation rate.' By implementing left-shifted quality testing, knowledge engineering, API specifications, and Half-Stack role restructuring, they achieved a 3x increase in effective code output per frontend developer, 2x for backend developers, and a 30%-55% reduction in defect rates.
